body: `should_strip_auth` is a security boundary. The only cross-origin case that may keep the Authorization header is http -> https on the same host with default ports. Any other change of host, scheme or port must strip it, and every new case needs a test in test_requests.py.
diff_hunk:
@@ -127,6 +127,10 @@ def should_strip_auth(self, old_url, new_url):
         old_parsed = urlparse(old_url)
         new_parsed = urlparse(new_url)
+        if old_parsed.hostname.endswith(new_parsed.hostname):
+            return False

body: In `rebuild_proxies`, always delete the old Proxy-Authorization header before deciding whether to add a new one. Otherwise credentials for one proxy leak to the next proxy after a redirect.
diff_hunk:
@@ -315,8 +315,6 @@ def rebuild_proxies(self, prepared_request, proxies):
         new_proxies = resolve_proxies(prepared_request, proxies, self.trust_env)
-        if "Proxy-Authorization" in headers:
-            del headers["Proxy-Authorization"]

body: Please don't let urllib3 exceptions escape `send`. Callers catch requests.exceptions only, so wrap the new error in ConnectionError (or the matching requests exception) with request=request, like the other except blocks here.
`get_netrc_auth` must not fail when ~/.netrc is broken or unreadable: skip netrc auth unless raise_errors is set. A bad netrc file would otherwise break every request on the machine.
diff_hunk:
@@ -240,7 +240,6 @@ def get_netrc_auth(url, raise_errors=False):
-        except (NetrcParseError, OSError):
-            if raise_errors:
-                raise
